problem:
Consider the expression $f(x,y)=-{x}^{3}y.$ What are the missing entries in the following sign table of $f(x,y)?$

| $y>0$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ |  |  |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |

feedback.problem:
Consider the expression $f(x,y)=-3{x}^{4}{y}^{7}.$ Fill the table with appropriate sign of $f(x,y)$ as shown below.

| $y>0$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=0.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040514/assets/5fd85410238231152b6f905921f594af15293d6efc54b0b1ce558131a05bf6ee.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040514/assets/e95107f16eb80a06cd172c30ec78992838f974a91f9f2fa17b7c8ac77125c438.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $-3{x}^{4}$ | ${y}^{7}$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-1,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-1,-1)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(1,-1)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |

 

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040514/assets/ff354ce9051d24e6f0adc4e0def143de86b36418b0b9846fdac1b4a63ca630f3.png)

Finally, we fill in the required sign table.

| $y>0$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ | $+$ | $+$ |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |
